title: Consideration of electromagnetic wave interference on microorganism inactivation on reflective surfaces
task: Quantify electromagnetic wave interference effects on microorganism inactivation near reflective surfaces
key_results: Thermal rise ΔT near metallic walls 1–2 orders of magnitude lower than interior (< 1 °C vs 30–100 °C); UV-C inactivation curves show saturation tails due to interference minima; interference minima persist at surfaces regardless of wavelength.
comments: While physically interesting, the practical sterilization implications depend heavily on pathogen location distribution and the penetration depth of interference patterns, which are not fully characterized.

model_io.model: Microwave thermal inactivation in oven cavity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Wave interference creates spatially stable exposure minima where pathogens can survive near reflective surfaces
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; inactivation curves saturate and thermal imaging shows persistent minima at walls

hypotheses.hypothesis: Thermal rise near cavity walls is orders of magnitude lower than interior due to interference minima
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ΔT < 1 °C near wall vs 30–100 °C interior in microwave experiments

title: Tubular tRF‑1:30‑Gln‑CTG‑4 attenuates tubulointerstitial fibrosis by mitigating FBXO7-mediated mitophagy defect in diabetic kidney disease
task: Define tRF-1:30-Gln-CTG-4 mechanism in attenuating tubulointerstitial fibrosis via mitophagy restoration
key_results: tRF-1:30-Gln-CTG-4 overexpression reduced fibrosis and restored mitophagy; tRF binds FBXO7 to prevent PINK1 ubiquitylation and degradation
comments: The identification of tRF-FBXO7-PINK1 axis is novel, though the therapeutic potential remains to be validated in clinical diabetic kidney disease models.

hypotheses.hypothesis: tRF-1:30-Gln-CTG-4 reduces TIF by inhibiting FBXO7-mediated PINK1 degradation
hypotheses.result: tRF overexpression attenuated fibrosis and restored mitophagy

hypotheses.hypothesis: FBXO7 promotes mitophagy defect through PINK1 ubiquitylation
hypotheses.result: FBXO7 elevation correlated with PINK1 degradation and mitophagy impairment

title: Chemotherapy-induced senescence promotes stroma stiffness and antioxidant adaptation to promote chemoresistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
task: Identify chemotherapy-induced senescence mechanisms driving stromal stiffness and chemoresistance in PDAC
key_results: Gemcitabine-induced tumor cell senescence activates CAFs; Piezo1-NRF2-BRG1 axis confers antioxidant-dependent gemcitabine resistance; senolytic-ferroptosis combination overcomes resistance in vivo
comments: The integration of mechanobiology with metabolic adaptation is mechanistically elegant, though the clinical translatability of ABT-263+Erastin combination requires further investigation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chemotherapy-induced senescence activates CAFs and increases matrix stiffness
hypotheses.result: Gemcitabine treatment induced fibrotic remodeling and increased stromal stiffness

hypotheses.hypothesis: Piezo1 signaling promotes NRF2-BRG1-dependent antioxidant adaptation
hypotheses.result: Matrix stiffness activated Piezo1, promoting NRF2 translocation and SLC7A11 upregulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Senolytic-ferroptosis combination dismantles chemoresistance
hypotheses.result: ABT-263+Erastin reduced tumor burden and enhanced T-cell infiltration in vivo

title: Single-cell technologies in mRNA cancer vaccines

key_results: Single-cell profiling enables characterization of immune cell subsets and intercellular communication; supports precision medicine development for tumor heterogeneity
comments: This is a review article providing framework rather than novel experimental findings; emphasis on methodological advancement rather than mechanistic discovery.

title: RBM15 impairs Hepatic Mitochondria and β-Oxidation through m6A-dependent degradation of MCM3 mRNA
task: Elucidate m6A-mediated regulation of hepatic mitochondrial function in diabesity
key_results: MCM3 overexpression improved mitochondrial function and β-oxidation; RBM15/YTHDF2 axis promoted m6A-dependent MCM3 mRNA decay via NRF2-KEAP1 axis
comments: The mechanistic link between m6A modification and metabolic dysfunction is well-established, though the reliance on db/db mice limits generalizability to human diabesity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RBM15 mediates MCM3 degradation via m6A-YTHDF2 axis
hypotheses.result: RBM15 overexpression accelerated MCM3 mRNA decay; knockdown reversed phenotype

title: A lightweight, integrated generative AI assistant for accelerated early-stage drug discovery on constrained-resource hardware
task: Cost-effective generative AI for small-molecule drug discovery on consumer hardware
key_results: LSTM-based generative model with SELFIES tokenization achieved training loss reduction from 2.15 to 1.19; toxicity classifier achieved weighted average AUC of 0.790; 93% infrastructure cost reduction versus enterprise solutions
comments: Practical engineering contribution democratizing drug discovery, though clinical validation of generated compounds remains pending.

hypotheses.result: Validated on benchmark tasks with stable convergence and reliable AUC metrics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid toxicity screening reduces false negatives in early-stage safety assessment
hypotheses.result: Toxic-class recall improved significantly after threshold tuning

title: Single cell and bulk transcriptomics reveal metabolic reprogramming biomarker signatures during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for cardiogenic shock
task: Identifying metabolic reprogramming biomarkers predicting ECMO outcomes in cardiogenic shock
key_results: Five biomarkers (PLIN2, TKTL1, NR1H4, GPX3, NNMT) associated with outcome prediction; TKTL1, NR1H4, NNMT showed significant differential expression (P < 0.05) between success/failure groups; monocytes identified as predominant cell type with dynamic biomarker expression trajectories
comments: Integrates bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, and clinical validation, though sample sizes and effect sizes not specified; doxorubicin molecular docking prediction lacks experimental confirmation.

monocyte differentiation trajectories with biomarker dynamics

title: Reinforcement learning for treatment decision-making in sepsis: a scoping review
task: Scoping review of reinforcement learning for sepsis treatment decision-making
key_results: 72 studies reviewed; 80.6% used MIMIC database; majority focused on vasopressor/fluid management; many RL policies outperformed clinician baselines, but evaluation method validity uncertain
comments: Identifies critical gap between retrospective promise and lack of prospective validation; reliability concerns are understated given absence of clinical trial evidence.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RL-derived sepsis treatment policies outperform clinician decisions
hypotheses.result: Many studies reported superior RL policies, but evaluation rigor and clinical validity remain uncertain

hypotheses.hypothesis: Standardized state/action/reward design improves generalizability across datasets
hypotheses.result: High variability in study design identified as barrier; future work should emphasize clinically guided standardization

title: Unsteady boundary-layer flow and radiative heat transfer over a deformable stretching cylinder with transpiration and slip: cross-validated Akbari-Ganji and finite-element solutions

comments: Mean-field calculations suggest robustness, but experimental verification of the proposed higher-Chern-number phases and non-Abelian quasiparticle physics remains crucial.

title: Escape-induced temporally correlated noise driven crossover in growth kinetics and universality class
task: Characterization of universality class crossover in thin-film growth driven by temporally correlated noise
key_results: Sharp dynamical crossover from Villain-Lai-Das Sarma (VLDS) scaling to adatom-escape-driven regime in Sn growth on Sb-doped MnBi₂Te₄; adatom escape identified as microscopic origin of temporally correlated noise causing universality class transition
comments: Atomically resolved experiments coupled with molecular dynamics provide mechanistic insight, though the generalizability of this noise mechanism to other growth systems requires exploration.

title: Imaging of gate-controlled suppression of superconductivity via the Meissner effect
task: Imaging gate-controlled suppression of superconductivity via Meissner effect in niobium nanostructures
key_results: Scanning nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry at sub-Kelvin temperatures reveals gate-controlled suppression of Meissner screening in niobium islands; observations consistent with quasiparticle hot-spot model, excluding Joule heating and electric field mechanisms
comments: Local magnetic imaging provides direct evidence of genuine superconductivity suppression beyond transport, though the practical scalability of the NV technique to device applications remains limited.

model_io.model: Niobium superconducting islands with gate electrode

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gate-controlled suppression manifests as reduced Meissner screening via quasiparticle generation

title: Rotational wobble effects on equilibrium structure and Floquet stability in the circular restricted three body problem
task: Analysis of rotational wobble effects on equilibrium structures and Floquet stability in the circular restricted three-body problem
key_results: Rotational wobble of the smaller primary (first-order perturbation) replaces classical libration points with time-dependent equilibria; Floquet analysis shows systematic stability spectrum modifications; cumulative trajectory deviations reach 10⁵–10⁶ m over extended periods for Sun–Earth system
comments: Perturbation-theoretic treatment is analytically elegant, but the model's validity beyond small wobble amplitudes and its relevance to realistic mission timescales require numerical investigation.

model_io.model: Extended circular restricted three-body problem with rotational wobble

hypotheses.hypothesis: Periodic rotational wobble of the smaller primary induces time-dependent perturbations and cumulative orbital deviations
hypotheses.result: Analytical perturbation theory predicts displaced equilibria; numerical simulations confirm 10⁵–10⁶ m deviations for Sun–Earth system over extended integration periods

title: Experimental and numerical study of the effect of appurtenances on the wind-induced vibrations of a cable-stayed bridge
task: Experimental and numerical assessment of appurtenances effects on wind-induced vibrations in cable-stayed bridges across construction and completion stages
key_results: Bridge shows stage-dependent aerodynamic sensitivity: completion phase exhibits 20% higher drag, 64% lower lift, 52% higher rolling moment compared to construction; vertical displacement/acceleration decrease by 79%/40% during construction; lateral acceleration increases 69% post-completion; critical flutter speed >108 m/s; soft flutter at -3° angle of attack
comments: Integrated wind-tunnel and stochastic simulation approach is comprehensive, though notable divergence between numerical and experimental results at high wind speeds for completed bridge suggests model limitations at extreme conditions.

model_io.model: Cable-stayed bridge aeroelastic model (construction and completion stages)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Appurtenances (railings, tracks, ancillary attachments) significantly alter aerodynamic and dynamic behavior between construction and completion stages
hypotheses.result: 20–64% changes in aerodynamic coefficients; lateral stability critically reduced post-completion; vertical stability worsened during construction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Soft flutter (rather than conventional flutter/galloping) governs aeroelastic stability at moderate angles of attack
hypotheses.result: Soft flutter observed at -3°; critical flutter speed >108 m/s well above design requirements

title: Design of topological thermal diffusion in the quasi ballistic phonon regime
task: Design of topological thermal diffusion in quasi-ballistic phonon transport regimes
key_results: Framework based on Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with size-dependent thermal conductivity successfully predicts decay rates of localized topological interface states in silicon nanostructures; experimental agreement validates effective model for nanoscale phonon transport
comments: The effective-conductivity parameterization elegantly bridges microscopic phonon ballistics and macroscopic diffusion theory, though universal applicability to diverse materials remains to be established.

model_io.model: SSH-based topological diffusion framework with effective thermal conductivity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Topological thermal diffusion with effective conductivity accurately describes nanoscale quasi-ballistic phonon transport
hypotheses.result: Predicted decay rates agree well with measured values, validating the effective-model approach for engineering topological heat management
